Marta R: Heads-up: saw a small but consistent NDCG@10 drop on the reranker after switching doc padding from 128 -> 256 tokens. Not huge, but shows up across multiple datasets. Anyone else noticing padding-related effects?

Owen G: Can you paste the eval numbers and run id so I can dig in?

Marta R: Pasting the minimal summary below (run ids trimmed). Full artifacts linked after.
```
Model           | pad_len | NDCG@10 | MRR@10
--------------- | ------- | ------- | ------
rerank-v3-fp16  | 128     | 0.423   | 0.361
rerank-v3-fp16  | 256     | 0.415   | 0.358
rerank-v3-ptq   | 128     | 0.418   | 0.359
rerank-v3-ptq   | 256     | 0.402   | 0.344
```
small delta for fp16, bigger for PTQ int8. run ids: eval/2024-04/4782, eval/2024-04/4783 (pad change).

eval-bot: New eval run queued: eval/2024-04/4784 (requested by Marta R)

Li W: Did we change tokenizer behavior or truncation side? Left/right padding or special tokens can shift positions and change the effective context window. Also PTQ kernels sometimes handle padding tokens differently (zeroing vs perf-optimized masking).

Marta R: We didn't change tokenizer config. Only change in the eval was pad_len from 128->256 in the harness config. Also tried the PTQ binary with `--int8` flag and observed larger drop.

Owen G: :thinking_face: Could be ranking tie-breaking from floating point noise after different key/value offsets. Can you share a query+doc example where ordering flips between 128/256?

Marta R: here's a minimal example where the rel label flips (sanitized):
Query: "how to rotate a tensor in pytorch"
Doc A: (short, 60 tokens) -> relevant
Doc B: (long, 340 tokens) + padded to 256 -> becomes longer; score_A > score_B at pad=128 but flips at pad=256 for ptq run.

Sasha P: Quick hypothesis: padding adds additional KV steps that shift the cached indices in the quantized kernels which use block-aligned buffers. Try forcing deterministic kernels + same seed and also run with `--pad_token_id 0` vs no padding to see if masking semantics differ.

Sasha P: Example eval command I would run: 
```
./eval_runner --model rerank-v3-ptq --pad_len 256 --seed 42 --deterministic-kernels true --output results_pad256.json
./eval_runner --model rerank-v3-ptq --pad_len 128 --seed 42 --deterministic-kernels true --output results_pad128.json
```

Marta R: Running those now (kickoff at 1708130300). Will post diff.

eval-bot: Run eval/2024-04/4784 started by Marta R

eval-bot: Run eval/2024-04/4784 completed. Summary: NDCG@10 0.404 (pad256, ptq, det kernels). See artifact: https://artifacts/reports/4784

Li W: If deterministic kernels remove the delta then it's likely a kernel-level instability interacting with padding. If not, could be masking vs attention normalization differences. Also check token type ids and any post-tokenization whitespace changes.

Owen G: For the write-up please capture: per-query flip list, NDCG delta by query length bucket, and the model config (quant flags, kernel version, tokenizer hash). That will make a clear signal to hand to infra/ops.

Marta R: Agreed. I'll produce a small CSV: query_id, pad128_score, pad256_score, flip_flag, token_len_doc. Also adding a synthetic stress slice with docs crafted to be sensitive to prefix shift.

Sasha P: If this reproduces, I'll add a unit test in the rerank eval harness: run both pad modes for a 100-sample synthetic slice and assert NDCG parity within epsilon. I'll open a PR. :thumbsup:

Marta R: Thanks — next steps: 1) rerun deterministic ptq (in progress), 2) diff per-query, 3) test masking semantics in runtime. I'll post artifacts when ready.

Owen G: Thanks Marta — flagging this for the triage doc.
